sentences.zh: 本，我们在周五早上和你连线，今天早上刚出炉了一堆糟糕透顶的经济数据。

sentences.en: So we wanted to sift through them with you.

sentences.en: Yeah, it's been a pretty dark morning for the economy.

sentences.en: Nearly 3 million more Americans filed for unemployment benefits last week.
sentences.zh: 上周又有近300万美国人申请失业救济。

sentences.en: When we learned that another 3 million Americans had filed for unemployment benefits.
sentences.zh: 当我们得知又有300万美国人申请了失业救济时。

sentences.en: That's more than 36 million people in two months.
sentences.zh: 两个月内这就是超过3600万人。

sentences.en: We're two months into this crisis, and yet we are still losing millions of jobs every week.
sentences.zh: 这场危机已经持续两个月了，然而我们每周仍在失去数百万个工作岗位。

sentences.en: For eight straight weeks now, jobless claims have been in the millions, with 3 million more people filing for unemployment last week.
sentences.zh: 失业救济申请人数已经连续八周达到数百万，上周又有300万人申请失业。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Every week.
sentences.zh: 每周都是如此。

sentences.en: Every week.
sentences.zh: 每周。

sentences.en: This did not happen naturally.
sentences.zh: 这不是自然发生的。

sentences.en: All of these companies didn't just go out of business because demand disappeared.
sentences.zh: 所有这些公司并不是因为需求消失而仅仅是倒闭了。

sentences.en: We turned our economy off.
sentences.zh: 我们按下了经济的暂停键。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: Think about New York.
sentences.zh: 想想纽约。

sentences.en: Think about the state of California.
sentences.zh: 想想加利福尼亚州。

sentences.en: If you ran a restaurant, a mini golf course, or a clothing store, there's a really good chance you would have laid your workers off.
sentences.zh: 如果你经营一家餐厅、一个迷你高尔夫球场或一家服装店，你很有可能会让员工失业。

sentences.en: And then, Friday morning, we get up.
sentences.zh: 然后，到了周五早上，我们醒来。

sentences.en: It's the services industries that are getting crushed here.
sentences.zh: 遭受重创的是服务业。

sentences.en: And we learn that retail sales in April were down more than 16%.
sentences.zh: 我们得知4月份的零售额下降了16%以上。

sentences.en: That's by far the worst that we've ever seen.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是有史以来最糟糕的情况。

sentences.en: But as far as these retail sales go, worse than expected, month over month.
sentences.zh: 但就这些零售额而言，环比跌幅比预期还要糟糕。

sentences.en: Over the last two months, restaurants lost half their business.
sentences.zh: 在过去的两个月里，餐厅失去了半数业务。

sentences.en: Apparel and clothing stores have lost nearly 90% of their business.
sentences.zh: 服装店的业务损失了近90%。

sentences.en: You know, the country's shut down and people aren't buying stuff.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，国家关闭了，人们也不买东西了。

sentences.en: I mean, I hate to state the obvious, but they're not buying cars down 12%.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我不喜欢说显而易见的话，但他们没有买车，销量下降了12%。

sentences.en: They're not buying furnishings and home furnishing items down 58%.
sentences.zh: 他们没有购买家具和家居用品，下降了58%。

sentences.en: Clothing and clothing accessories down 78%.
sentences.zh: 服装及衣着附件下降了78%。

sentences.en: And then we got another data point that said that industrial production, right, this is the actual
sentences.zh: 然后我们得到了另一个数据，显示工业生产，对吧，这是我们在经济中实际

sentences.en: stuff that we make in the economy, was down by the most in the more than a century that we've been keeping records.
sentences.zh: 制造的东西，其降幅创下了我们有记录一个多世纪以来的之最。

sentences.en: Meaning worse than the Great Depression.
sentences.zh: 这意味着比大萧条时期还要糟糕。

sentences.en: In other words, as bad as it gets.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，糟糕透顶。

sentences.en: As bad as it has ever gotten.
sentences.zh: 这是有史以来最糟糕的情况。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: We know that this is deep.
sentences.zh: 我们知道这是深层次的。

sentences.en: We know that it is broad-based.
sentences.zh: 我们知道这是广泛的。

sentences.en: We don't yet know how long it will laSt. And that's the fundamental question going forward.
sentences.zh: 我们还不知道它会持续多久，而这是未来的根本问题。

sentences.en: So, given all that, I want to turn to a speech.
sentences.zh: 所以，鉴于这一切，我想谈谈一场演讲。

sentences.en: Good morning.
sentences.zh: 早上好。

sentences.en: It's my pleasure and privilege to welcome back Chair Jay Powell.
sentences.zh: 我非常荣幸和高兴地欢迎杰伊·鲍威尔主席再次莅临。

sentences.en: That the chairman of the Federal Reserve, Jerome Powell, made a couple of days ago.
sentences.zh: 这是美联储主席杰罗姆·鲍威尔几天前发表的讲话。

sentences.en: That I think speaks to all this data.
sentences.zh: 我认为这番话切中了所有这些数据。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And, of course, the chairman of the Federal Reserve doesn't make a ton of speeches.
sentences.zh: 当然，美联储主席并不常发表公开演讲。

sentences.en: So, I know that his words carry a lot of weight.
sentences.zh: 所以，我知道他的话分量很重。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, Jerome Powell comes out.
sentences.zh: 于是，杰罗姆·鲍威尔登场了。

sentences.en: The coronavirus has left a devastating human and economic toll in its wake.
sentences.zh: 冠状病毒留下了毁灭性的人员伤亡和经济代价。

sentences.en: Of course, he's giving the speech remotely.
sentences.zh: 当然，他是通过远程方式发表讲话的。

sentences.en: So, he's sort of in front of these blue curtains, or maybe they're digitally superimposed blue curtains.
sentences.zh: 所以，他有点像是站在这些蓝色窗帘前面，或者也许它们是数字合成的蓝色窗帘。

sentences.en: I'm not actually sure.
sentences.zh: 我其实不太确定。

sentences.en: On a Zoom-style call.
sentences.zh: 在类似 Zoom 的通话中。

sentences.en: But he comes out with this really stark message.
sentences.zh: 但他带着这样一个非常严峻的信息出场了。

sentences.en: The scope and speed of this downturn are without modern precedent.
sentences.zh: 这次经济衰退的规模和速度在现代是没有先例的。

sentences.en: And he's saying, this economic crisis is incredibly deep.
sentences.zh: 他在说，这场经济危机极其深重。

sentences.en: We are seeing a severe decline in economic activity and employment.
sentences.zh: 我们看到经济活动和就业率急剧下降。

sentences.en: It's incredibly broad.
sentences.zh: 它是极其广泛的。

sentences.en: And already the job gains of the last decade have been erased.
sentences.zh: 过去十年的就业增长已经荡然无存。

sentences.en: And it is hitting the most vulnerable workers more than anyone.
sentences.zh: 而且它对最脆弱的工人的打击超过了任何人。

sentences.en: He has this line early in the speech where he says, While we're all affected.
sentences.zh: 他在演讲早期有这样一句话，他说，虽然我们都受到了影响。

sentences.en: While we are all affected.
sentences.zh: 虽然我们都受到了影响。

sentences.en: The burden has fallen most heavily on those least able to bear it.
sentences.zh: 但负担最重地落在了那些最无力承担的人身上。

sentences.en: The burden has fallen most heavily on those least able to bear it.
sentences.zh: 负担最重地落在了那些最无力承担的人身上。

sentences.en: Among people who were working in February, almost 40 percent of those in households making less than
sentences.zh: 在2月份有工作的人中，家庭年收入低于

sentences.en: $40,000 a year had lost a job in March.
sentences.zh: 4万美元的人里，有近40%在3月份失去了工作。

sentences.en: Lower income Americans, Black Americans, less educated Americans.
sentences.zh: 低收入美国人、黑人美国人、受教育程度较低的美国人。

sentences.en: But the coronavirus crisis raises longer term concerns as well.
sentences.zh: 但冠状病毒危机也引发了更长期的担忧。

sentences.en: The record shows that deeper and longer recessions can leave behind lasting damage to the productive capacity of the economy.
sentences.zh: 历史表明，更深、更长的经济衰退可能会对经济的生产能力留下持久的损害。

sentences.en: And Ben Powell talks about this specter of permanent economic damage in this speech.
sentences.zh: 本，鲍威尔在这次演讲中谈到了这种永久性经济损害的幽灵。

sentences.en: And perhaps he was referring most urgently to these lower income workers.
sentences.zh: 也许他最急迫指的是这些低收入工人。

sentences.en: But I want to understand that concept because it feels a little bit new to me.
sentences.zh: 但我想理解这个概念，因为对我来说这感觉有点新鲜。

sentences.en: I think of almost all economic conditions as temporary.
sentences.zh: 我几乎把所有的经济状况都视为暂时的。

sentences.en: So what did he mean by that?
sentences.zh: 那么他到底是什么意思？

sentences.en: You're right to think about most economic conditions as temporary because historically that is the way economists have thought about recessions and economic downturns.
sentences.zh: 你认为大多数经济状况是暂时的这没有错，因为从历史上看，经济学家对衰退和经济低迷就是这样看的。

sentences.en: is some people lose their jobs and then they get those jobs back when things get better.
sentences.zh: 即一些人失去了工作，然后在情况好转时又重新得到了工作。

sentences.en: Some businesses lose business or maybe they go out of business, but other things come back up and replace them.
sentences.zh: 一些企业失去了业务，或者可能倒闭了，但其他事物会重新出现并取代它们。

sentences.en: But we've learned over time that that is not the way recessions always work, and especially long and deep recessions.
sentences.zh: 但随着时间的推移，我们了解到经济衰退并不总是那样运作的，尤其是长期和深度的经济衰退。

sentences.en: That when people lose their jobs, if they're out of work for too long, they can drift away from the labor
sentences.zh: 当人们失去工作时，如果他们失业时间过长，他们可能会脱离劳动力

sentences.en: market, they can lose their connections, and all of a sudden, even when the economy starts to get better, it's very hard for them to get back to work.
sentences.zh: 市场，他们可能会失去联系，突然之间，即使经济开始好转，他们也很难重返工作岗位。

sentences.en: I wonder if you can give me an example of this to kind of bring it to life.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你能否给我举个例子，让它变得生动一点。

sentences.en: Well, imagine a small company, right, that maybe somebody has spent their lives, maybe a couple generations building.
sentences.zh: 嗯，想象一下一家小公司，对吧，也许有人花了一生时间，也许几代人建立起来的。

sentences.en: You can imagine if this crisis were to last a few weeks, they lose some revenue, they take a hit, but they start right back up where they left off.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象，如果这场危机持续几周，他们失去了一些收入，受到了打击，但他们会在离开的地方重新开始。

sentences.en: But as this drags on and they fall behind on loans, you fall behind on your rent payments,
sentences.zh: 但随着时间的拖延，他们的贷款落后了，房租支付落后了，

sentences.en: and all of a sudden, you can get to a place where you can't reopen that business, where you can't restart.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，你可能会发现自己无法重新开业，无法重新开始。

sentences.en: And sure, the business owner might be able to go and find another job, but that business is lost forever.
sentences.zh: 当然，企业主或许可以去找另一份工作，但那个企业永远消失了。

sentences.en: And so that is what Powell is referring to when he talks about permanent economic damage from this pandemic.
sentences.zh: 这就是鲍威尔在谈到这场大流行造成的永久性经济损害时所指的。

sentences.en: That's what Powell fears, and that's what he wants to make sure we avoid.
sentences.zh: 这就是鲍威尔所担心的，也是他希望确保我们能避免的。

sentences.en: What kind of solution, what kind of plan does he have in mind in this speech to avoid permanent economic damage?
sentences.zh: 为了避免永久性的经济损害，他在演讲中提出了什么样的解决方案，什么样的计划？

sentences.en: Well, Powell starts by talking about all the things that we have already done, and he's full of praise for that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，鲍威尔首先谈到了我们已经做过的事情，他对这些赞不绝口。

sentences.en: The response here in the United States has been particularly swift and forceful.
sentences.zh: 美国这里的应对措施特别迅速和有力。

sentences.en: He talks about what the Fed itself has done, of course, but he also talks about...
sentences.zh: 他当然谈到了美联储自己所做的事情，但他也谈到了……

sentences.en: To date, Congress has provided roughly $2.9 trillion.
sentences.zh: 迄今为止，国会已经提供了大约2.9万亿美元。

sentences.en: What Congress has done, the nearly $3 trillion in emergency spending that Congress has approved.
sentences.zh: 国会所做的事情，国会批准的近3万亿美元的紧急支出。

sentences.en: For households, businesses, healthcare providers, and state and local governments.
sentences.zh: 为了家庭、企业、医疗保健提供者以及州和地方政府。

sentences.en: And there are a lot of programs that Congress has enacted to try to deal with this, right?
sentences.zh: 国会为了应对这一情况已经颁布了许多计划，对吧？

sentences.en: They've written checks to virtually every American.
sentences.zh: 他们给几乎每个美国人都开具了支票。

sentences.en: They've offered loans and grants to businesses.
sentences.zh: 他们向企业提供贷款和赠款。

sentences.en: And Powell says that all of those things have been incredibly important to softening the blow of this crisis.
sentences.zh: 鲍威尔表示，所有这些事情对于缓和这场危机的打击都极其重要。

sentences.en: The overall policy response to date has provided a measure of relief and stability and will provide some support to the recovery when it comes.
sentences.zh: 迄今为止的整体政策应对提供了一定程度的救济和稳定，并将在复苏到来时为其提供一些支持。

sentences.en: But then he says...
sentences.zh: 但接着他说……

sentences.en: But the coronavirus crisis raises longer-term concerns as well.
sentences.zh: 但冠状病毒危机也引发了更长期的担忧。

sentences.en: Basically, we're not done yet.
sentences.zh: 基本上，我们还没完呢。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: That that was not enough.
sentences.zh: 这还不够。

sentences.en: That it probably won't be enough.
sentences.zh: 这可能还不够。

sentences.en: That we know now that this is not a crisis that is going to last for just a month or just a couple of months.
sentences.zh: 我们现在知道，这不是一场只持续一个月或几个月的危机。

sentences.en: It's going to drag on.
sentences.zh: 它将会拖延下去。

sentences.en: And that as it drags on, if the government doesn't step in and do enough to keep people and businesses afloat, then we're going to see a lot more of that kind of permanent
sentences.zh: 随着它的拖延，如果政府不介入并采取足够的措施来维持人民和企业的生计，那么我们将看到更多鲍威尔所谈论的那种永久性

sentences.en: damage that Powell is talking about.
sentences.zh: 损害。

sentences.en: And when he suggests that we aren't done yet, what is he really saying?
sentences.zh: 当他暗示我们还没完时，他真正想表达的是什么？

sentences.en: What he's really saying is to Congress, you need to keep spending.
sentences.zh: 他真正想对国会说的是，你们需要继续支出。

sentences.en: The Fed will do what it can do.
sentences.zh: 美联储会尽其所能。

sentences.en: But the Fed can only lend money.
sentences.zh: 但美联储只能借钱。

sentences.en: It's Congress that has the ability to spend money, to give money to people, to give money to businesses.
sentences.zh: 只有国会有能力花钱，把钱给人民，把钱给企业。

sentences.en: And that is, in all likelihood, what it will take to get through this period.
sentences.zh: 按所有可能性来看，这就是度过这段时期所需要的。

sentences.en: He describes what's been done so far as a bridge, a bridge across temporary interruptions, he says.
sentences.zh: 他将目前所做的事情描述为一座桥梁，一座跨越暂时性中断的桥梁，他说。

sentences.en: And what he's basically saying is the bridge doesn't yet reach all the way across the river.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是在说，这座桥还没有完全延伸到河的对岸。

sentences.en: And a bridge doesn't do you much good if it stops when you're still over water.
sentences.zh: 如果桥在你还在水面上时就停下来了，那对你也没什么大用。

sentences.en: No, it does not.
sentences.zh: 不，确实没用。

sentences.en: I mean, is that normal for the chairman of the Fed to do this, to be advising Congress to spend a lot more money in this manner?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，美联储主席这样做是正常的吗，以这种方式建议国会花更多的钱？

sentences.en: Not in as direct terms as this.
sentences.zh: 没有这么直接的说法。

sentences.en: But this was, at least by the standards of Fed chairs, a pretty direct call to action.
sentences.zh: 但至少按美联储主席的标准来看，这是一个相当直接的行动呼吁。

sentences.en: Additional fiscal support could be costly, but worth it if it helps avoid long-term damage and leaves us with a stronger recovery.
sentences.zh: 额外的财政支持可能是代价高昂的，但如果它有助于避免长期损害并让我们迎来更强劲的复苏，那就是值得的。

sentences.en: This trade-off is one for our elected representatives, who wield powers of taxation and spending.
sentences.zh: 这种权衡是我们的民选代表的事，他们掌握着税收和支出的权力。

sentences.en: And can we safely assume that when the chairman of the Federal Reserve tells Congress, this is what I think you should do, that he assumes that that is what Congress will do?
sentences.zh: 我们可以安全地假设，当美联储主席告诉国会，这就是我认为你们应该做的时，他假定国会就会这么做吗？

sentences.en: Oh, I don't think we should assume that Powell thinks that Congress will do it.
sentences.zh: 哦，我认为我们不应该假设鲍威尔认为国会会这么做。

sentences.en: But I think Powell knew that he was speaking at a moment when there's a major political
sentences.zh: 但我觉得鲍威尔深知，他是在这样一个时刻发表讲话的：民主党人和共和党人

sentences.en: debate that's playing out between Democrats and Republicans about what the role of government is in this crisis.
sentences.zh: 正在这场危机中就政府应扮演何种角色展开激烈的政治辩论。

sentences.en: And he's, in effect, weighing in on one side of that debate, but I don't think he's under any illusion that he alone will resolve it.
sentences.zh: 而他实际上是在为这场辩论的一方站台，但我认为他并不幻想自己能独自解决这个问题。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》App？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 已解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果能免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需绑定信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在可以了。

sentences.en: When you download The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》App时，你在该App内的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你尚未订阅《纽约时报》，请立即下载《时报》App，即可免费畅读30天。

sentences.en: So Ben, describe the divisions between Democrats and Republicans in Congress about this advice from Jerome Powell, the chairman of the Federal Reserve.
sentences.zh: 那么，本，请介绍一下国会中的民主党人和共和党人，对于美联储主席杰罗姆·鲍威尔提出的这项建议有何分歧。

sentences.en: Well, think back for a moment to those trillions of dollars in spending that have already taken place.
sentences.zh: 好的，回想一下不久前已经投入的那数万亿美元支出。

sentences.en: I want to highlight a few areas of bipartisan economic relief we will be voting on today.
sentences.zh: 我想强调我们今天将要投票表决的几个两党经济纾困领域。

sentences.en: Recovery checks to give Americans needed cash to provide for their families.
sentences.zh: 救助支票为美国人提供必需的现金来养家糊口。

sentences.en: When Congress approved those measures, it was really bipartisan.
sentences.zh: 当国会批准这些措施时，确实得到了两党支持。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: This is a strange and evil disease.
sentences.zh: 这是一种奇怪而邪恶的疾病。

sentences.en: There is much we still don't know about it.
sentences.zh: 关于它，我们仍有许多未知。

sentences.en: And it is keeping us apart.
sentences.zh: 它让我们彼此隔离。

sentences.en: But that came at a moment when the economy was in the process of shutting down.
sentences.zh: 但那是发生在经济正处于关闭状态的时刻。

sentences.en: And there was pretty widespread agreement that that had to happen.
sentences.zh: 而且大家对必须这么做有着相当广泛的共识。

sentences.en: When we pass this bill, instead of hugging each other, we'll wave from a distance.
sentences.zh: 当我们通过这项法案时，我们将不再拥抱彼此，而是在远处挥手。

sentences.en: None of us can know when this plague will pass.
sentences.zh: 我们没有人知道这场瘟疫何时会过去。

sentences.en: The only thing we know for sure is that we must summon the same spirit that saw previous generations through America's darkest hours.
sentences.zh: 我们唯一能确定的就是，我们必须唤起那种曾陪伴历代美国人度过最黑暗时刻的精神。

sentences.en: We're now in a very different moment.
sentences.zh: 我们现在处于一个非常不同的时期。

sentences.en: Jeff Craig, leader?
sentences.zh: 杰夫·克雷格，领袖？

sentences.en: Well, it's been two weeks since Leader McConnell called us back into session.
sentences.zh: 好吧，自从麦康奈尔领袖召集我们复会以来已经过去两周了。

sentences.en: Where there are real divisions between Republicans and Democrats about how quickly reopening should take place.
sentences.zh: 共和党人和民主党人对于应该以多快速度重新开放，存在真正的分歧。

sentences.en: In that time, it was announced that 30 million Americans filed for unemployment.
sentences.zh: 在此期间，据宣布有3000万美国人申请了失业救济。

sentences.en: And yet the Republican leader has scheduled exactly zero votes, zero, on legislation related to the corona crisis.
sentences.zh: 然而，共和党领袖针对与新冠危机相关的立法，恰好安排了零次、零次投票。

sentences.en: And with that comes real disagreement about the role of the federal government in continuing to support businesses and especially workers.
sentences.zh: 随之而来的是，对于联邦政府是否应继续支持企业尤其是工人，存在着真正的分歧。

sentences.en: Let's solve the problem right now.
sentences.zh: 让我们现在就解决这个问题。

sentences.en: What are we going to do for people who are out of work?
sentences.zh: 我们要为失业的人做些什么？

sentences.en: The Democrats are by and large saying much of the country is still shut down.
sentences.zh: 民主党人总的来说认为，全国大部分地区仍然处于关闭状态。

sentences.en: What are we going to do for businesses that are going under?
sentences.zh: 我们要为那些濒临倒闭的企业做些什么？

sentences.en: And so the government has to continue to support workers and businesses.
sentences.zh: 因此政府必须继续支持工人和企业。

sentences.en: It has to keep on spending.
sentences.zh: 它必须继续支出。

sentences.en: The Republican side is a little more complicated.
sentences.zh: 共和党方面的立场要复杂一些。

sentences.en: This emergency is very serious.
sentences.zh: 这场紧急情况非常严重。

sentences.en: So the Senate's response has been serious.
sentences.zh: 因此参议院的反应也是严肃的。

sentences.en: It's not unanimous.
sentences.zh: 这不是一致通过的。

sentences.en: But there is certainly, at least in Congress, more of an inclination to say...
sentences.zh: 但至少在国会中，确实有更多的倾向认为……

sentences.en: Look, here in the real world, Senate Republicans are working seriously to help the country reopen.
sentences.zh: 看吧，在现实世界中，参议院共和党人正在认真努力地帮助国家重新开放。

sentences.en: Let's see how this reopening process goes.
sentences.zh: 让我们看看这个重新开放的过程进展如何。

sentences.en: Let's see if the businesses reopen.
sentences.zh: 让我们看看企业是否会重新开业。

sentences.en: And if they do, maybe we don't need to do very much more.
sentences.zh: 如果它们开业了，也许我们就不需要做更多的事情了。

sentences.en: And if they don't come back and there's a need for further action, then we can talk about that then.
sentences.zh: 如果它们没有恢复营业，并且需要进一步采取行动，那么我们到那时再谈。

sentences.en: So it's a bit more of a wait and see whether Congress really needs to spend all that much more money.
sentences.zh: 因此，这更像是一种观望态度，看国会是否真的需要花那么多钱。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that question of spending is what's hanging over this, that Republicans are looking at the trillions with a T that have been spent so far and saying, can we wait to spend more?
sentences.zh: 而这种关于支出的问题正是笼罩在此之上的阴云，共和党人看着目前已经花掉的以“万亿”计的资金，在说：我们能等等再花更多钱吗？

sentences.en: The crushing unemployment figures show us that no amount of federal spending could substitute for the entirety of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 惨淡的失业数据向我们表明，任何数量的联邦支出都无法完全替代整个美国

sentences.en: economy.
sentences.zh: 经济。

sentences.en: We need to be smart and we need to be safe.
sentences.zh: 我们需要保持明智，我们需要确保安全。

sentences.en: But we have to find a more sustainable middle ground.
sentences.zh: 但我们必须找到一个更具可持续性的折中方案。

sentences.en: Ben, how tied are these different approaches to the kind of longstanding economic ideologies of the Democratic and Republican parties?
sentences.zh: 本，这些不同的方法与民主党和共和党长期以来的经济意识形态有多大联系？

sentences.en: Well, look, Republicans have a longstanding discomfort with programs like unemployment insurance.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你看，共和党人对失业保险之类的项目长期以来一直感到不安。

sentences.en: At a certain point, these benefits are going to do more harm than good.
sentences.zh: 在某个时间点，这些福利带来的弊端将大于益处。

sentences.en: And I would say they already are starting to do that.
sentences.zh: 而且我要说，它们其实已经开始产生这种影响了。

sentences.en: So extending unemployment benefits through next year would deter people from trying to return to work because why would they?
sentences.zh: 因此，将失业救济延长到明年将会阻止人们尝试重返工作岗位，因为他们为什么要这样做呢？

sentences.en: Why would someone choose to do more work for less money?
sentences.zh: 为什么会有人选择拿更少的钱去做更多的工作呢？

sentences.en: So it's not surprising that as we move from the acute phase of this crisis into the long,
sentences.zh: 所以毫不奇怪，当我们从这场危机的急性期过渡到漫长而

sentences.en: slow recovery, that Republicans would be the first to start raising questions about the spending and to start thinking about pulling back on some of those prograMs.
sentences.zh: 缓慢的复苏期时，共和党人会率先开始对支出提出质疑，并开始考虑削减其中一些项目。

sentences.en: So we're already looking at staggering debt that we are going to have to deal with at some point
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在正面临着惊人的债务，我们总得在某个时候去处理它

sentences.en: because it's immoral to expect our kids and grandkids to pay that money back after we've already cashed those checks.
sentences.zh: 因为在我们已经兑现了那些支票之后，指望我们的子孙后代来偿还这笔钱是不道德的。

sentences.en: Democrats have long advocated for more generous unemployment benefits, for a larger role for government.
sentences.zh: 民主党人长期以来一直主张更慷慨的失业福利，主张政府发挥更大的作用。

sentences.en: And so it's not too surprising that they are more comfortable with these programs lasting longer.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们对这些项目持续更长时间感到更加适应，也就不足为奇了。

sentences.en: We need to show that we have a government that understands the scale of this problem and understands that the approach to it is to get money down into the hands of the people
sentences.zh: 我们需要表明，我们的政府了解这个问题的规模，并知道应对它的方法是将资金下发到

sentences.en: who will put it down at the grassroots level and help support this economy from the ground up.
sentences.zh: 那些能够在基层使用它并从底层开始支持这个经济的人手中。

sentences.en: And so this is the longstanding, very inflexible, ideological terrain that Howell is entering when he goes to Congress and says, hey, cough up trillions of dollars more.
sentences.zh: 因此，这就是鲍威尔去国会说“嘿，再掏出几万亿美元”时，所踏入的那个长期存在的、非常僵化的意识形态地带。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But it feels like in this debate, the real anxiety is over just the enormity of the scale of money that we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 但感觉在这场辩论中，真正的焦虑其实是对我们所谈论的庞大资金规模的担忧。

sentences.en: And I feel at this point, I have to ask you the question that we all kind of pretend to know the answer to, which is, where does all this money come from that Powell is suggesting
sentences.zh: 我觉得在这一点上，我不得不问你那个我们大家都假装知道答案的问题，那就是：鲍威尔建议

sentences.en: Congress spend and that Democrats and Republicans are not really agreeing on whether to spend?
sentences.zh: 国会花钱、而民主党和共和党又没有真正达成一致是否要花的这所有钱，究竟是从哪里来的？

sentences.en: In the simplest terms, we're borrowing it.
sentences.zh: 用最简单的话说，我们是借来的。

sentences.en: The Congressional Budget Office projects that the deficit this year will be $3.7 trillion.
sentences.zh: 国会预算办公室预计今年的赤字将达到3.7万亿美元。

sentences.en: And we're borrowing those trillions of dollars from whom?
sentences.zh: 我们向谁借了这数万亿美元？

sentences.en: So Congress decides how much it's going to spend.
sentences.zh: 所以国会决定它要花多少钱。

sentences.en: And it, of course, sets tax rates as well.
sentences.zh: 当然，它也设定了税率。

sentences.en: And any time that Congress decides to spend more than it brings in in tax rates, then the Treasury Department has to sell bonds to make up the difference.
sentences.zh: 每当国会决定支出的资金超过其税收收入时，财政部就必须出售债券来弥补差额。

sentences.en: And that just means that it's asking people, investors, foreign governments to lend the United
sentences.zh: 这仅仅意味着它在要求人们、投资者、外国政府向美国

sentences.en: States money.
sentences.zh: 借钱。

sentences.en: You give us money now, we'll give you money back with a small amount of interest in anywhere from a few days to 10 years.
sentences.zh: 你们现在给我们钱，我们在几天到10年不等的期限内连本带利地还给你们一小笔利息。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So when we hear about Treasury bonds and their yields, that is the interest payment that the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们听到国债及其收益率时，那就是美国

sentences.en: government is giving to someone who buys a Treasury bond and in the process has kind of lent money to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 政府给购买国债的人的利息支付，在这个过程中，他们实际上把钱借给了美国

sentences.en: and to Congress.
sentences.zh: 和国会。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Every time the government sells a bond, it's borrowing money from the public.
sentences.zh: 政府每次出售债券，都是在向公众借钱。

sentences.en: It's paying some interest on that.
sentences.zh: 它为此支付一定的利息。

sentences.en: Just like if you borrowed money to buy a house or to make a purchase, to buy a car.
sentences.zh: 就像你为了买房、进行消费或买车而借钱一样。

sentences.en: The only difference is the federal government gets a much better interest rate than you or I ever will.
sentences.zh: 唯一的区别是，联邦政府获得的利率比你我所能获得的要好得多。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: So we kind of become the bank.
sentences.zh: 所以我们有点变成银行了。

sentences.en: We become the bank.
sentences.zh: 我们变成了银行。

sentences.en: And to hear someone like Jerome Powell describe it, that doesn't seem all that risky for Congress to spend all that money, which would require the U.S.
sentences.zh: 听杰罗姆·鲍威尔这样的人描述，国会花那么多钱似乎并不是那么冒险，这需要美国

sentences.en: borrowing that much from us and anyone who wants to buy U.S.
sentences.zh: 向我们以及任何想买美国

sentences.en: Treasury bonds.
sentences.zh: 国债的人借那么多钱。

sentences.en: But is it risky?
sentences.zh: 但这有风险吗？

sentences.en: So in the short term, there's really no risk here.
sentences.zh: 所以在短期内，这里确实没有任何风险。

sentences.en: We can keep borrowing as long as people will keep lending us money.
sentences.zh: 只要人们还愿意借钱给我们，我们就可以继续借下去。

sentences.en: In the long term, of course, we have to make good on those loans.
sentences.zh: 当然，从长期来看，我们必须履行这些贷款的承诺。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And we have to pay interest on those loans.
sentences.zh: 而且我们必须为这些贷款支付利息。

sentences.en: And so there will certainly be a debate when we come out the other side of this crisis about what the government should do about these huge deficits.
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们走出这场危机的另一端时，肯定会就政府应该如何处理这些巨额赤字展开辩论。

sentences.en: But that debate is still years away because we're at a very particular moment right now, which is that we're in the middle of an immediate crisis.
sentences.zh: 但这场辩论还要等上好几年，因为我们现在处于一个非常特殊的时刻，那就是我们正处于眼前的危机之中。

sentences.en: And if we don't get our economy back on track, then none of that longer run debate matters.
sentences.zh: 如果我们不能让我们的经济重回正轨，那么所有这些长期的辩论都将毫无意义。

sentences.en: That debate is conditional on having an economy economy at all on the other side of this.
sentences.zh: 这场辩论的前提是，在这场危机的另一端，我们必须首先得有一个经济体。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So you could have an economy with little debt, but you might not have much of an economy at all.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以拥有一个负债很少的经济体，但你可能根本没有什么像样的经济体。

sentences.en: Yeah, Powell is saying the debt is the least of our worries right now.
sentences.zh: 是的，鲍威尔在说债务是我们目前最不担心的事。

sentences.en: It's not that it doesn't matter.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说它不重要。

sentences.en: It's not that it will never matter.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说它永远不会重要。

sentences.en: But we have to try to get the economy through this period and moving again before we can worry about any of those other long run concerns.
sentences.zh: 但在我们担心任何其他长期担忧之前，我们必须努力让经济度过这段时期并再次运转起来。

sentences.en: You could think about it like performing CPR, right?
sentences.zh: 你可以把它想象成做心肺复苏，对吧？

sentences.en: Performing CPR often involves breaking ribs.
sentences.zh: 做心肺复苏通常伴随着断肋骨。

sentences.en: And that's a real consequence.
sentences.zh: 这是一个真实的后果。

sentences.en: But that doesn't mean you don't perform CPR.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着你不做心肺复苏。

sentences.en: You perform
sentences.zh: 你做

sentences.en: CPR, you try to get somebody's heart started again, and then you worry about the other consequences once the person's heart is beating again.
sentences.zh: 心肺复苏，试图让某人的心脏重新跳动，然后一旦这个人的心脏再次跳动，你再去担心其他后果。

sentences.en: And just to be clear in this metaphor, the broken ribs is massive U.S.
sentences.zh: 为了在这个隐喻中把话说清楚，断了的肋骨就是美国巨额的

sentences.en: debt spending on stimulus.
sentences.zh: 刺激性债务支出。

sentences.en: And the heart is the American economy, which right now is stopped and which we somehow have to get beating again.
sentences.zh: 而心脏则是美国经济，它现在已经停止跳动，而我们无论如何都必须让它重新跳动起来。

sentences.en: And so what you now have is Powell and lots of other economists who, like him, would normally be worried about the debt, who are saying now is not the moment.
sentences.zh: 所以你现在看到的是，鲍威尔以及许多其他像他一样、通常会担心债务的经济学家都在说，现在不是时候。

sentences.en: That includes people who were advisors to George W.
sentences.zh: 这包括曾担任乔治·W·

sentences.en: Bush, people who were advisors to
sentences.zh: 布什顾问的人，以及在过去几十年里担任

sentences.en: Republican candidates and Republican leaders throughout the last several decades.
sentences.zh: 共和党候选人和共和党领袖顾问的人。

sentences.en: Pretty much all of the economists that I talk to and that my colleagues have been talking to are saying the same thing, which is now is not the moment to worry about the debt.
sentences.zh: 几乎所有与我交谈过以及与我的同事交谈过的经济学家都在说同样的话，那就是现在不是担心债务的时候。

sentences.en: So if this is the broad consensus of economists across the United States, Ben, why is this much of a debate in Congress at all?
sentences.zh: 因此，如果这是美国各地经济学家的广泛共识，本，为什么这在国会里还会引起这么大的辩论？

sentences.en: I mean, economists like to think that they issue these sage pieces of advice and everybody on Capitol Hill and in state houses will rush to follow them.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，经济学家喜欢认为他们发布了这些明智的建议，国会山和各州议会大厦里的所有人都会争先恐后地去听从。

sentences.en: But of course, that's not the way the world works.
sentences.zh: 但当然，世界不是这样运转的。

sentences.en: And so it may well be the case that many members of Congress thank the Federal Reserve chairman, but say, you know, we're not going to follow that advice.
sentences.zh: 因此，很有可能许多国会议员感谢了美联储主席，但却说：“你知道，我们不会遵循这个建议。”

sentences.en: And we've already heard Republicans in Congress saying exactly that.
sentences.zh: 而且我们已经听到国会中的共和党人这样说了。

sentences.en: Look, I mean, we can't spend enough money to prop this economy up forever.
sentences.zh: 听着，我的意思是，我们不可能花足够多的钱来永远支撑这个经济。

sentences.en: People need to be able to begin to be productive again, consistent with the guidelines that have been laid down by the healthcare professionals toward opening up the economy.
sentences.zh: 人们需要能够重新开始进行生产，这要符合医疗专业人员为开放经济所制定的指导方针。

sentences.en: It's the only solution to the dilemma with which we are confronted.
sentences.zh: 这是解决我们所面临困境的唯一出路。

sentences.en: They just don't believe that what Powell is saying right now is the real solution to our economic
sentences.zh: 他们只是不相信鲍威尔现在所说的是解决我们经济

sentences.en: problems, even though many of their own economic advisors are telling them the same thing.
sentences.zh: 问题的真正方案，尽管他们自己的许多经济顾问也在对他们说同样的话。

sentences.en: Ben, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 本，非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他内容。

sentences.en: I'm so proud of you, Davey.
sentences.zh: 我为你感到骄傲，戴维。

sentences.en: Thousands of high school and college seniors across the country.
sentences.zh: 全国各地成千上万的高中和大学应届毕业生。

sentences.en: Yeah, congratulations.
sentences.zh: 是的，恭喜。

sentences.en: Good job.
sentences.zh: 干得好。

sentences.en: Good summer.
sentences.zh: 祝暑假愉快。

sentences.en: Celebrated their graduation over the weekend in virtual ceremonies.
sentences.zh: 在周末通过线上虚拟仪式庆祝了他们的毕业。

sentences.en: Happy graduation, Matt.
sentences.zh: 毕业快乐，马特。

sentences.en: And were toasted in commencement speeches by everyone from Oprah Winfrey to Tom Hanks.
sentences.zh: 从奥普拉·温弗瑞到汤姆·汉克斯，每个人都在毕业典礼的演讲中向你们致敬。

sentences.en: You are the chosen ones.
sentences.zh: 你们是天选之人。

sentences.en: You are the chosen ones because of a fate unimagined when you began your Wright State adventures.
sentences.zh: 你们之所以是天选之人，是因为你们经历了一种在开启莱特州大冒险时无法想象的命运。

sentences.en: You started in the olden times and the world back before the great pandemic of 2020.
sentences.zh: 你们开始于远古时代，也就是2020年大流行爆发之前的世界。

sentences.en: You will talk of those earlier years in your lives just that way.
sentences.zh: 你们以后谈起生活中那些早年时光，就会用这种语气。

sentences.en: Well, that was back before the COVID-19.
sentences.zh: “哦，那是新冠疫情之前的事了。”

sentences.en: In his commencement speeches, former President Barack Obama delivered pointed criticism of how the U.S.
sentences.zh: 在前总统巴拉克·奥巴马的毕业典礼演讲中，他尖锐地批评了美国

sentences.en: government has handled the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 政府应对这场大流行的方式。

sentences.en: More than anything, this pandemic has fully, finally torn back the curtain on the idea that so many of the folks in charge know what they're doing.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，这场大流行彻底且最终地扯下了遮羞布，粉碎了“许多掌权者知道自己在做什么”这种想法。

sentences.en: A lot of them aren't even pretending to be in charge.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人甚至连装都不装了。

sentences.en: Obama did not mention President Trump by name, but his remarks were seen as a clear indictment of his successor.
sentences.zh: 奥巴马虽然没有点名道姓地提到特朗普总统，但他的言论被视为对其继任者的明确谴责。

sentences.en: Now, all those adults that you used to think were in charge and knew what they were doing,
sentences.zh: 现在，所有那些你曾经以为是掌权且知道自己在做什么的成年人，

sentences.en: turns out they don't have all the answers.
sentences.zh: 结果发现他们并非掌握了所有答案。

sentences.en: A lot of them aren't even asking the right questions.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人甚至连正确的问题都没问。

sentences.en: So if the world's going to get better, it's going to be up to you.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果世界要变得更好，就要靠你们了。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 《每日新闻》节目到此结束。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》节目中，我们将为假期接待客人做好准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人宾至如归的秘诀。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们对光线敏感吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they black out to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是不是喝断片了才睡觉。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们需要什么样的光线条件？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢喝咖啡还是茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》App或你喜欢的任何播客平台上搜索《Wirecutter秀》。
